findings.issue: Index 183 keys a single full-credit answer, Secreções (“descrever a secreção, caso presente, incluir aspecto e quantidade”), for an utterance about dry yellowish crusts found when cleaning the nose, with liquid explicitly denied (“Não sai líquido correndo, só esses pedacinhos”). The source entry is conditional on a secretion being present. The source does not say that crusts are recorded as secretion, none of the 204 contexts mentions crusts, the story's evidence cites no reference, and its rationale states the inclusion as a decision (“achado válido para a entrada Secreções”). The other four Secreções stories in scope describe moist material.

source.locator: ÓRGÃOS DOS SENTIDOS > NARIZ E SEIOS PARANASAIS: > Secreções

evidence.quote: Secreções: descrever a secreção, caso presente, incluir aspecto e quantidade

findings.resolution: Held as doubtful. No un-keyed term fits better (running is denied, no blood, no blocked nose), so the question is only whether the keyed term is clearly correct. A student may reasonably read the utterance as “no secretion present”. The reviewer opened no external source that would settle it; it is a teaching decision.
findings.requiredStoryChange: Not rewritten by the reviewer. Either (a) a teaching reviewer confirms that dry nasal crusts are scored as Secreções, in which case the story can be released as keyed; or (b) the story is rewritten to describe a secretion that is present (moist material with aspect and quantity) or removed. A rewritten story needs a new independent review.

findings.issue: Indices 170–179 (Rinorreia stories) and 181 and 184 (Secreções stories) give full credit to both Rinorreia (“Coriza, nariz escorrendo”) and Secreções (“descrever a secreção, caso presente, incluir aspecto e quantidade”). The second entry is an instruction to characterise the discharge rather than a separate symptom, so every runny-nose utterance that says what the liquid looks like and how much there is ends up with two correct answers.

ÓRGÃOS DOS SENTIDOS > NARIZ E SEIOS PARANASAIS: > Secreções

evidence.quote: Secreções: descrever a secreção, caso presente, incluir aspecto e quantidade

findings.resolution: Passed. The reviewer finds both paths supported by the sentence itself: liquid running from the nose is nasal secretion in ordinary usage, each utterance states that it is present and gives its aspect, and all but two give a clear amount (see B016-05). The batch applies the rule consistently: every in-scope utterance with outflow keys both terms, and the ones where outflow is denied key Secreções only. It remains a key-design choice; a teacher may prefer Rinorreia alone for plain watery discharge. Teaching confirmation recommended before clinical approval.

findings.issue: The source describes Obstrução nasal as “nariz entupido, dificuldade de respirar”, which overlaps the Dispneia descriptions (“sensação [subjetiva] de dificuldade ou desconforto para respirar”, printed under the respiratory and the cardiovascular headings). The batch draws the line by an explicit clause: indices 165, 166, 167 and 169 state comfortable or normal mouth breathing (or deny breathlessness) and key Obstrução nasal only; index 168 adds a feeling of not getting enough air and uncomfortable breathing and keys Obstrução nasal plus both Dispneia entries (so does index 164, out of scope).

evidence.text: O nariz parece vedado e mal consigo puxar ar por ele. Mesmo abrindo a boca, continuo com uma sensação incômoda de não conseguir ar suficiente.

findings.resolution: Passed. In the four single-key stories Dispneia is not equally supported because the patient says breathing is fine apart from the nose. In index 168 the feeling of lacking air is stated in the patient's own words and matches both Dispneia lines almost literally. Question for the teacher: should shortness of breath reported together with a blocked nose also score Dispneia, and in particular APARELHO CARDIOVASCULAR > Dispneia, given that the Obstrução nasal line already contains “dificuldade de respirar”?

findings.issue: Indices 180 and 182 describe thick white or greenish material that comes out only on blowing the nose and key Secreções without Rinorreia. “Coriza” in everyday use can include thick catarrh, so a student might also pick Rinorreia.

evidence.text: O que tiro do nariz no lenço é uma pequena porção de muco transparente, mais grosso que água. Não fica escorrendo, só aparece quando assoo.

findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the key: both utterances deny running in so many words (“não escorre sozinho”; “não corre por si”), and the source glosses Rinorreia as “nariz escorrendo”. The batch uses the same rule at index 186 (out of scope). Question for the teacher: should thick discharge obtained only by blowing the nose also count as Rinorreia?

findings.issue: The Secreções entry asks for aspect and quantity. Indices 174 and 177 give the aspect (“água clara”; “líquido transparente”) but the amount only indirectly (drops that fall before the tissue is reached; “Continua pingando”). The other ten dual-key utterances state an amount (several tissues, a soaked tissue, several drops, several times a day).
findings.resolution: Passed: the secretion is present and described, which is what the entry is about, and the full-credit question is the same as B016-02. If the teacher keeps the dual key, a later edit could add an explicit amount to these two utterances.

findings.issue: Each story's rationale and each evidence rationale was read against its own utterance. None names a symptom, term or detail belonging to another story. Two leftovers of shared template text were found in the stories' own alternativeAssessment field: the five Secreções stories (180–184) carry the sentence “A descrição de sangue, quando presente, também recebe Epistaxe”, although none of them mentions blood (it applies to index 185, out of scope); and the four single-key Obstrução nasal stories carry the group sentence about Dispneia credit that applies to index 168. The rationale of index 168 speaks of “os dois caminhos de Dispneia” without naming Obstrução nasal as the third path.

evidence.text: Ao assoar, saiu um pouco de material branco com sangue vermelho misturado. Era grosso, e vi claramente o sangue no que saiu do nariz.

findings.resolution: No story is affected: the template sentences are conditional (“quando presente”, “Quando a fala também declara…”) and do not assert anything false about the utterance. Editorial observation only.

findings.issue: The term stage is easy. Rinorreia utterances use escorre/pinga/corre, close to the source's “nariz escorrendo” (index 176 says “Meu nariz escorre”). All single-key Obstrução nasal utterances end with a clause about breathing well through the mouth, and the Secreções-only utterances with a clause denying running; these clauses are what separates the keys, but they also work as a tell. Technical terms never appear in the utterances.
findings.resolution: Within the stated rules (lay speech, one or two paragraphs, technical term not given away). Editorial observation only.

findings.issue: The references attached to these stories (mesh-nasal-obstruction, mesh-rhinorrhea, mesh-dyspnea) were not re-opened by this reviewer. In the Rinorreia stories the Secreções evidence cites mesh-rhinorrhea; in the Secreções stories the Secreções evidence cites no reference at all.
findings.resolution: This review judges the term matching against the source script only. Reference verification remains with the batch's own review metadata; the missing reference for the crust story is part of B016-01.

withheld.reason: A fala descreve “um material amarelado e seco, em pequenas casquinhas”, visto ao limpar o nariz, e nega líquido (“Não sai líquido correndo, só esses pedacinhos”). O gabarito aceita apenas Secreções. Não encontrei termo fora do gabarito que caiba melhor: o escorrimento é negado pela fala, não há sangue, nariz fechado nem dor, e o roteiro não tem entrada para crostas nasais. A dúvida é se o único termo do gabarito está claramente sustentado. A entrada manda “descrever a secreção, caso presente”; a fala descreve crostas secas e diz que não sai líquido. Crosta pode ser secreção ressecada, mas a fala não diz isso, e uma estudante pode concluir, com razão, que não há secreção presente a descrever. A própria justificativa da história apresenta a inclusão como decisão (“achado válido para a entrada Secreções”), sem apoio no texto da apostila e sem referência citada. As outras quatro falas do grupo descrevem material úmido (grosso, pegajoso, muco, líquido). Não consigo afirmar que Secreções seja a resposta claramente correta aqui; item retido para decisão docente ou reescrita. Forma: fala leiga em um parágrafo, sem termo técnico.
